summary: This article explains how gravity pulls objects together, keeps us on the ground, sets our weight, holds the Moon and planets in orbit, and causes tides.
introduce: Drop a pencil and ask, “What was the cause? What was the effect?” to model the idea quickly. Then show the title “Gravity: What Keeps Us on the Ground” and tell students to look for things in the article that make other things happen.

keyTerms.def: the amount of matter, or stuff, in something
the path one thing takes as it goes around and around another thing

challengeTerms.def: a force that pulls two things toward each other
a scientific explanation, supported by evidence, of how something in nature works
a space that contains almost no air or other matter

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that gravity is the most important force in our everyday lives? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain how gravity affects both the Moon and Earth's oceans.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review mass, attract, and orbit, and let weak readers match cause cards to effect cards from the article with a partner.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses attraction, theory, and vacuum to explain one important cause-and-effect chain from the article.
